question: What is the meaning of maintenance in relation to instructions for use, maintenance, and end-of-life treatment?
data_group: instructions for use, maintenance, and end-of-life treatment
description: Maintenance refers to the activities carried out to ensure the proper functioning and longevity of a product. In the context of instructions for use, maintenance, and end-of-life treatment, maintenance includes the adjustment and maintenance operations that should be carried out by the users, as well as the preventive maintenance measures that should be observed. It also involves the type and frequency of inspections and the maintenance required for reasons of safety and durability, including the criteria for replacement of parts subject to wear. Additionally, maintenance encompasses the necessary actions to be taken in the event of product failure or accident during use, as well as the recommendations for repair, deinstallation, reuse, remanufacturing, recycling, and safe deposit. Overall, maintenance aims to maintain the performance of the product during its service life span and mitigate risks beyond the basic points of use, maintenance, and end-of-life treatment.

3.3. Proposed framework to enable dynamic information flow
The literature review indicates that current DPP development lacks
focus on updating information during the maintenance phase by third-
party service providers. To address this gap, we propose a blockchain-
based DPP system design that facilitates dynamic information flow
and ensures secure and effective updates, particularly for maintenance
information provided by third-party service providers during the prod-
uct use phase. Given the limited emphasis in the literature on post-
launch data inclusion mechanisms, our proposal highlights the impor-
tance of incorporating user verification and authorization within the
blockchain-based DPP system.
Based on the findings in Section 4, the core requirements for this
framework include data source, data carrier, data security, and user
access and verification. Since the data source involves third-party ser-
vice providers, a blockchain-based DPP is suitable to enhance data se-
curity and trust in data sharing, as it has been widely adopted in DPP
initiatives. Smart contracts can be used to verify the identity of service

3.3.1. Framework explanation
To address the data collection of maintenance service by 3rd party
service provider during the launch of the product of DPP, we proposed
conceptual framework consists of several key components such as the
DPP and user management illustrated in. Our framework enables the
updating of maintenance history (e.g. condition-based maintenance/
repair) by 3rd party service provider. This information is important for
recyclers/manufacturers to understand recycling or circularity potential
and support decisions making at the end of life of a product.
The DPP should use a unique identifier so that all data generated
throughout the product life cycle can be associated with it. ID man-
agement is a central aspect of DPP management. When a DPP is created,
a unique ID (e.g., a URL) will be assigned to the DPP to ensure that the
DPP can be updated and accessible throughout all the product life cycle
phases. We propose the use of standards, such as GS-1 Digital Link (GS1,
2023), to ensure globally identifiable, unique IDs. This is crucial for data
consistency in a decentralized system. In addition, a product tag that
contains a data carrier such as QR codes or RFIDs will be used to link
physical products with their DPPs. A scanning app (e.g., a mobile QR
code reader) can then be used to retrieve and update the DPP data.
A key component in our framework is the role of blockchain tech-
nology. Blockchain can provide an immutable record of events, ensuring
that every update, transaction, or change is recorded in chronological
order.

2.3. Maintenance needs with a view to maintaining the performance of the product during its service life span:
(a) description of the adjustment and maintenance operations that should be carried out by the users and the 
preventive maintenance measures that should be observed;
(b) the type and frequency of the inspections and the maintenance required for reasons of safety and durability and, 
where appropriate, the parts subject to wear and the criteria for replacement;
(c) information on what to do in the event of product failure or accident.
2.4. Safety during use:
(a) instructions on the protective measures to be taken by the user, including, where appropriate, the personal 
protective equipment to be provided;
(b) instructions designed for the safe use of the product, including the protective measures that should be taken 
during its use;
(c) information on what to do in the event of product failure or accident during use.
2.5. Training and other requirements necessarily to be fulfilled for safe use.
2.6. Risk mitigation possibilities going beyond points 2.1 to 2.5.
2.7. Recommendations for a product’s:
(a) repair;
(b) deinstallation;
(c) reuse;
(d) remanufacturing;
(e) recycling;
(f) safe deposit.
2.8. Where applicable, information on the performance of the product as measured in terms of its climate change effects – 
total, as referred to in point (a) of Annex II, and human toxicity, cancer, as referred to in point (q) of Annex II.
3.
The information provided on the elements listed in point 2 shall be enough, both in terms of quantity and quality, to 
enable potential purchasers to make informed decisions before proceeding with their purchase, including information 
on the necessary quantity, installation, use, maintenance, dismantling, reuse and recycling of the respective product. It 
may include all the drawings, diagrams, descriptions and explanations necessary for it to be understood.
The information shall, as appropriate, take into account as far as possible the needs of designers, building authorities, 
construction professionals, building control authorities, consumers and other users, occupant and, use managers, as 
well as of maintenance professionals.
4.
Guidelines and technical details issued in accordance with Article 9(2) shall also recommend where the respective 
information is to be provided. That location shall be one where the information is least likely to be overlooked.
